column1: # Which recipe made which set of recordings.
# rederive-ref.sh reads this file, keyed by the census named in ../step.tsv, and
# builds the pinned command from the row. It is a table rather than a constant
# in the script because the three steps authored so far are graded against three
# different sets of recordings, taken on three different trees at two different
# rungs, and a script that pinned one of them shipped beside the other two would
# be a recipe that cannot produce the answers it sits next to.
# Columns:
#   census   the directory name under build/ the recordings came from, and the
#            value of the `census` row in the payload's step.tsv.
#   rung     the row of build/pkg/verifier/rungs.tsv the recordings were taken
#            at. Not necessarily the step's own rung: step 1 grades at rung 02
#            and is compared against recordings taken at rung 00, because
#            nothing it is scored on moves between the two.
#   spark    the Spark *distribution* in that image -- what $SPARK_HOME holds,
#            which is what actually runs a job. It is not the pom's
#            <spark.version>: spark-core is `provided` scope here, so the jar is
#            shaded without it and the engine comes from the image whatever the
#            pom says. rederive-ref.sh asserts this inside the container, off
#            $SPARK_HOME/jars/spark-core_<scala>-<spark>.jar, before it runs a
#            single job. That assertion is the whole reason this file exists:
#            the same jobs at the wrong rung produce a full set of plausible
#            recordings that differ from these in two places.
#   scala    the Scala binary version of that distribution, from the same name.
#   jdk      the JDK major version in the image.
#   ladder   the steps whose solution/solve.sh, applied to the baseline commit
#            in order, produce the tree the recordings come back off. `-` means
#            the untouched baseline.
#   image    the authoring tag the recordings were actually taken in. Any image
#            at the same rung will do -- the step's own verifier image is one,
#            and is the one a reader of the package can build, from the tests/
#            directory this file ships inside -- so this is a default for IMAGE
#            rather than a requirement. The requirement is the rung, and the
#            rung is asserted.
#   note     what the row is, in one line.
# census

column8: the 140-job version census at step 4's rung; ANSI is on in the ladder tree and off in these recordings, and c05b vs c05ansi is SAME=140 after projection (NOTES 6.4.1), so the ladder reproduces what is compared and moves two raw lines that determinism.tsv already declares

the 141-job version census at step 5's rung, the far end of a three-axis span (Scala 2.13, JDK 17, Spark 3.4.4); its first 140 jobs are decomposed rung by rung in NOTES 6.5.1 as SAME=138 with one VALUE difference on the JDK rung and one rc difference on the Spark rung, so every scored difference among them has a named axis. The 141st, HarnessDriver-csvdates, is where this row's ladder is load-bearing rather than documentary: spark-core is `provided`, so an inferring csv read has already moved to DateType at this rung whatever the tree says, and only the step-5 golden tree -- which pins preferDate=false at all six such reads -- reproduces the `timestamp` recorded here. It was taken off that tree (build/c09gold2), which reproduced the other 140 as 138 byte-identical and 2 declared VALUE in determinism.tsv, so the two provenances agree wherever they overlap
